clue.text: Walk, run, climb using this

parts.note: to step is to walk, a pace at a time
a ladder is a run in tights or stockings, a British usage

explanation.surface: A list of exercises: walk, run, then climb with some piece of equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' reads as jogging, but here it is a ladder, the British word for a run in a pair of tights.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepladder is a folding frame with treads that a person climbs to reach high places.

clue.text: Work as printer in family firm

parts.note: a type is a kind or class, like a family of related things
set means firm, as a jelly that has set

explanation.surface: Someone runs the printing press in the family business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'family firm' looks like one business, but the two words split into separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To typeset is to arrange type for printing, the compositor's job in a print shop.

clue.text: Support for piano

parts.note: pro is Latin for 'for', as in pros and cons
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: Something that holds up a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop is a post or beam that holds something up, a physical support.

clue.text: Untruth maintained by Capone's associates

indicators.note: something maintained by another is held up within it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Al Capone, the gangster; Al's gives ALS
an untruth is a lie

explanation.surface: A lie kept going by the gangster Al Capone's henchmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Allies are partners joined in a common cause, so they are associates.

clue.text: Gift provided by party people

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
a nation is a people sharing a country

explanation.surface: A present supplied by those attending a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation is something given freely, usually to a charity, so it is a gift.

clue.text: Drive-thru screens are fascinating

indicators.note: to screen is to conceal, so these words keep the answer concealed within them

explanation.surface: The display boards at a fast-food drive-through are captivating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screens' looks like a noun for display panels, but it is a verb saying the words conceal the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that rivet you hold your attention completely, so they are fascinating.

clue.text: Extremely safe medical scan

parts.note: ultra means extremely, as in ultra-modern
sound means safe, as in safe and sound

explanation.surface: A medical scan that is very safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultrasound imaging uses high-frequency sound waves to picture inside the body, a common hospital scan.

clue.text: Covers ring with one large layer of earth

parts.note: tops are lids or covers
O is ring-shaped
I is the Roman numeral one
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Something that covers a ring with one big layer of soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Topsoil is the uppermost stratum of soil, the fertile ground that gardeners dig.

clue.text: Huge demo turns nasty around the middle of Whitehall

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the other piece, enclosing it
the protest turning nasty suggests disorder, so these letters are rearranged
Whitehall has nine letters, and its central one is taken

explanation.surface: A massive protest march turns ugly in the heart of Whitehall, the London street of government ministries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reads as the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'nasty' signals the rearrangement. 'around' puts TREMNDOUS, the anagram of DEMOTURNS, around E.
explanation.definitionFit: Tremendous means very great in size or amount, so it is a synonym for huge.

clue.text: Vehicle reversing by a line of boats

indicators.note: a vehicle reversing goes backwards, so the word's letters run the other way

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A van backing up beside a row of boats.
explanation.definitionFit: Naval is the adjective for a navy and its ships, so it describes things relating to boats.

clue.text: Drugs reportedly provide relief

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the clue goes by how the letters are spoken

parts.note: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, so drugs are Es

explanation.surface: Drugs are said to give relief from pain.
explanation.walkthrough: Es, plural of E for ecstasy, is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease is to relieve pain or worry, so it means provide relief.

clue.text: One willing to try schedule after turning back

indicators.note: the turned piece comes after the first piece

parts.note: to test is to try out

indicators.note: turning back means the word for the schedule is read in reverse

parts.note: a rota is a schedule of duties

explanation.surface: Someone keen to test a timetable after going back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning back' makes ATOR from ROTA. 'One willing' reads as someone eager, but means someone making a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is a person who makes a will, so punningly one who is 'willing'.

clue.text: Where to take off and dry football kit

parts.note: to air laundry is to dry it
a team's strip is its football kit, a British term

explanation.surface: A place to remove and dry football kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' suggests undressing, which fits the football kit, but it means aircraft leaving the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An airstrip is a basic runway from which aircraft take off and land.

clue.text: Call for nurse before onset of tummy trouble

parts.note: EN stands for Enrolled Nurse

indicators.note: the onset is the start, so the word's first letter is taken

parts.note: to ail is to trouble, as illness does

explanation.surface: Calling for a nurse when a stomach ache begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail is to involve or require as a consequence, so it means call for.

clue.text: Plenty of dogs free from lead

indicators.note: a dog free from its lead is let loose; here the word loses its leading letter

parts.note: poodles are dogs

explanation.surface: Lots of dogs running off the leash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free from lead' takes the leading P from POODLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Oodles is an informal word for a large amount, so it means plenty.

clue.text: Study finishing early without the material

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps around the other
finishing early means the word stops short of its last letter

parts.note: to learn is to study

explanation.surface: Studying ends early without the right material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as 'lacking', but here it carries its old sense of outside; 'finishing early' leaves LEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather is tanned animal hide, a material used for shoes and bags.

clue.text: Despite that 50/50 bet, nothing!

parts.note: evens are betting odds where the stake is matched, a fifty-fifty chance
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A gambler bets at evens and wins nothing despite it all.
explanation.definitionFit: Even so is an idiom meaning nevertheless, so it means despite that.

clue.text: Contemptuous father going back inside shabby bar

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a dive is a shabby, disreputable bar

indicators.note: going back means the word for father is read in reverse

parts.note: a sire is a father

explanation.surface: A scornful father returns to a seedy bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Derisive means showing mockery or scorn, so it is a synonym for contemptuous.

clue.text: Artist put up prices

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: to set something down is to put it

explanation.surface: An artist raised what they charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SET into TES in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Rates are charges or fees, so they are prices.

clue.text: Some asparagus needed for Italian sauce

indicators.note: only some of the word is used, so the answer lies within it

explanation.surface: A little asparagus is wanted for an Italian sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragù is a meat-based Italian pasta sauce, as in ragù alla bolognese.

clue.text: At first, my intention's not truthfully to make money

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of each of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone claims that, to begin with, they did not intend to get rich dishonestly.
explanation.definitionFit: To mint is to stamp coins, literally making money.

clue.text: Complete power stripped from club

indicators.note: stripped from means one letter is removed from the word for the club

parts.note: a putter is a golf club
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A golf club totally lacks power.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter means absolute or total, as in utter nonsense, so it is complete.

clue.text: Made beastly noise, tangled in hedge

indicators.note: tangled means twisted up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A horse caught in a hedge whinnied in distress.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse neighed when it made its characteristic whinny, an animal's noise.

clue.text: Sports fans drink beers

parts.note: to sup is to drink
porter is a dark beer, so porters are beers

explanation.surface: Sports fans having a few drinks of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters are followers who cheer on a team, so they are sports fans.
